name: io.github.vike-io/vike-trader
title: vike-cli
description: Backtest, validate and execute trading strategies behind a mandatory two-call preview gate.

_vike.comment: OUR block, not the registry's. `tools` is held equal to `tools_spec` — ORDER INCLUDED, because that is the order tools/list returns — by `the_registry_manifest_lists_every_tool_this_server_serves` in crates/vike-cli/src/cmd/mcp.rs, which also holds `version` equal to the crate version the server reports at initialize. It lives at the top level rather than under `_meta` deliberately: the schema's own `_meta` slot is keyed by an upstream-chosen name (`io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided`), and a drift gate keyed on an upstream field stops checking the day that field is renamed. The schema sets no `additionalProperties: false` on ServerDetail, so this validates; if a future revision does, this block moves into that `_meta` slot and the gate's pointer moves with it.
_vike.write_tools_are_preview_gated: Every tool below carrying destructiveHint executes ONLY against a preview_token this server issued, unexpired, and bound to the same command. `confirm: true` on its own returns a preview and sends nothing. The token is not a secret: it proves a preview HAPPENED FOR THIS COMMAND — a sequence, not an authorization.
_vike.packages_deliberately_absent: No `packages` entry: this server ships as a Rust binary from the repository's own GitHub releases, not from npm/pypi/oci/nuget/mcpb, and naming a registry artifact that does not exist would be a guess. Choosing a distribution is part of the (unmade) decision to publish this listing at all.
